papers.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
papers.abstract: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to FL(3), the free lattice on three generators; this answers a question that R. A. Dean asked and the second author's 1997 notes on the problem left open. Every such chain would yield, inside FL(3), a coherent chain of proper self-embeddings $\Theta_0, \Theta_1, \Theta_2, \dots$ with $\Theta_k \circ \Theta_j = \Theta_j$ for $j < k$, so that each later embedding fixes the image of each earlier one pointwise. Every proper self-embedding of FL(3) whose fixed sublattice contains a free generating triple fixes one of the three generators, say $z$, because a power of it or of its dual lies above the identity, and a self-embedding that moves every generator and lies above the identity fixes at most eleven elements. Up to duality, a proper self-embedding fixing the image of such a $\Theta_1$ pointwise fixes only elements above $z \wedge (x \vee y)$, where no free generating triple containing $z$ can lie. We also verify the one-step example of the 1997 notes, prove that no step toward such a chain is self-similar, and show that the configuration the argument rules out at length three does occur at length two. Without freeness the answer reverses: FL(3) contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of 3-generated sublattices, so the lattice analogue of Takahasi's chain condition for free groups fails. The theorem itself is checked by the Agda proof assistant under its safe flags, for free lattices over generators with decidable equality, and its formal proof uses no classical principle: finite searches and an induction on a finite set replace the infinite pigeonhole principle by which a chain yields a coherent chain.

papers.title: Generalized Power Graph of a Group
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of graphs, called generalized power graphs, and investigate some of their key properties, such as completeness, connectivity, and planarity.

papers.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
papers.abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f$ and $Q_f$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free and that the canonical inner augmentation of a classical knot quandle is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot, whereas for every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$ it is free.

papers.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.

papers.title: Hierarchical hyperbolicity of Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: We show that for every finite rank Coxeter system, the Coxeter group is hierarchically hyperbolic relative to its nonhyperoctahedral irreducible higher rank affine parabolic subgroups. This is sharp---the Coxeter group admits a hierarchically hyperbolic group structure if and only if it has no such parabolic subgroups, and we give a complete diagrammatic characterization of when this is true. Moreover, this condition is equivalent to the existence of a coarsely equivariant coarse median on the Coxeter group. We also show that the Coxeter group is virtually a colorable hierarchically hyperbolic group. This is achieved by passing to a congruence subgroup of the Tits representation. As consequences, the Davis complex is a hierarchically hyperbolic space and the group admits a coarse median of rank equal to its algebraic rank. Furthermore, the Coxeter group is quasimedian quasiisometric to a finite dimensional CAT(0) cube complex and is virtually coarsely injective. Two appendices prove results of independent interest that are not Coxeter-specific. The first promotes a relative HHS structure with HHS peripheral coordinate spaces to an HHS structure. The second shows that a virtually Abelian group admits a coarsely equivariant coarse median precisely when it is hyperoctahedral.

papers.title: CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes, Bipodality and the Parallel Wall Property
papers.abstract: Coxeter cell complexes are a simultaneous generalization to cube complexes and the Davis complex of a Coxeter group. We show that 1-skeleta of CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes isometrically embed into a CAT(0) cube complex. When the resulting cube complex is finite dimensional, we show that the condition of bipodality (satisfied by both CAT(0) cube complexes and Davis complexes of Coxeter groups) implies local finiteness of the cubulation. To this end, we show a Parallel Wall Theorem for bipodal CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes satisfying a uniform bound on the size of a collection of pairwise intersecting walls. In particular, our methods give a new, purely geometric proof of the Parallel Wall Theorem for Coxeter groups.

papers.title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $\chi(1)_p$ of $\chi(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $\chi$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2\pi i/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $\chi_P$ is the restriction of $\chi$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $\chi_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: Products of Trees, $\Sigma$-theory, Higher Baumslag-Solitar Groups
papers.abstract: We study the $\Sigma$-theory of groups equipped with multiple HNN decompositions in the case where the product of the associated Bass-Serre trees satisfies the hypotheses of Brown's criterion. We then obtain an explicit description of the $\Sigma$-theory restricted to the span of all characters dual to one of the HNN decompositions. One consequence is that Meinert's Direct Product Formula holds in this context. As a key ingredient for the proof, we present a purely topological result that allows reading off the essential connectedness and acyclicity properties of products of regular trees with height functions. As the main application of our theorem, we introduce higher Baumslag-Solitar groups. We prove that they admit a canonical system of HNN decompositions, and use it to deduce multiple results, such as the existence of normal forms, and a well-behaved structure of standard parabolic subgroups (which include the vertex and edge groups). By understanding their interplay with a special class of endomorphisms called multiplication maps (which include the structure maps), we control the action on the product of Bass-Serre trees. This allows us to compute the full $\Sigma$-theory of higher Baumslag-Solitar groups.

papers.title: Universal Spaces for Coarsely Light Maps
papers.abstract: Coarsely light maps were introduced by Dydak--Weighill as a large-scale analogue of light maps. We show that a proper metric space has asymptotic dimension at most $n$ if and only if it admits a coarsely light map to $\mathbb R^n$. As an application, we resolve two questions of Benjamini--Schramm--Tim\'ar concerning semi-regular maps.

papers.title: Representing in Low rank II: Virtual structure and Isomorphism problem
papers.abstract: We group theoretically characterise the finite groups $G$ and number fields $F$ such that all $F$-representations of reduced degree at least $2$ are so-called exceptional. If $G$ is not a $2$-group, we obtain a full classification. Secondly, we determine whether such groups are uniquely determined by their group algebra $FG$. In particular, we obtain an instance of the virtual structure problem of Kleinert and answer the rational isomorphism problem for such groups.

papers.title: On four problems from the Kourovka Notebook: spectra, periodic automorphism groups, commutators, and operator simplicity
papers.abstract: We examine Problems 18.62(a), 18.63, 18.65, and 20.120 of the Kourovka Notebook. First, a family of semidirect products involving $\operatorname{PSL}_2(p^2)$ gives arbitrarily many pairwise nonisomorphic groups critical with respect to one simple-group spectrum, subject to explicit arithmetic congruences. Second, a completed-algebra construction using sparse torsion identities and a matrix Golod-Shafarevich-Vinberg inequality produces an infinite periodic group generated by two fixed-point-free automorphisms of order five of an abelian group. Third, we give a short matrix proof that the class of elements of order three in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ contradicts the assertion in Problem 18.65 as written. Finally, we spell out how P. Hall's 1962 wreath-power theorems answer Problem 20.120 under the usual normal-subgroup meaning of simplicity for a group with one distinguished automorphism. The four arguments have substantially different provenance. In particular, the last is a consequence of a known construction, not a priority claim. The two longer constructions are recorded in detail for independent mathematical scrutiny.

papers.title: $F$-congruences on $F$-inverse monoids
papers.abstract: We study the class of congruences on $F$-inverse monoids that respect the unary operation $a\mapsto\mx{a}$, assigning to each element the maximum element of its $\sigma$-class, which we refer to as $F$-congruences. We characterize kernel normal systems and congruence pairs on $F$-inverse monoids which give rise to such congruences and establish a number of further related results including a classification of $F$-congruence-free $F$-inverse monoids.

papers.title: Minimal Systems of Binomial Generators for the Ideals of Certain Monomial Curves
papers.abstract: Let $a, b$ and $n > 1$ be three positive integers such that $a$ and $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j$ are relatively prime. In this paper, we prove that the toric ideal $I$ associated to the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $\{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j\} \cup \{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j + a\, \sum_{j=0}^{i-2} b^j \mid i = 2, \ldots, n\}$ is determinantal. Moreover, we prove that for $n > 3$, the ideal $I$ has a unique minimal system of generators if and only if $a < b-1$.

papers.title: Positivity, cross-ratios, photons, and the Collar Lemma
papers.abstract: We prove that $\Theta$-positive representations of fundamental groups of surfaces (possibly cusped or of infinite type) satisfy a collar lemma, and their associated cross-ratios are positive. As a consequence we deduce that $\Theta$-positive representations form closed subsets of the representation variety. Along the way we systematically study a class of curves inside general flag manifolds that we call photons. Using their interplay with transversality in the flag manifold, we construct photon projections, which we use to relate the cross-ratios on the photons to the cross-ratios on the flag manifolds.

papers.title: Extensibility and denseness of periodic monoid actions
papers.abstract: A monoid has the periodic approximation (PA) property if, for every full shift on a finite alphabet, finitely supported invariant probability measures are weak-* dense in the space of invariant Borel probability measures. We introduce the class of measure-theoretically extension-compatible (MEC) monoids, consisting of embeddable monoids for which every probability measure-preserving (p.m.p.) action admits an invertible p.m.p. extension. For an embeddable monoid $S$ with free $S$-group $(\Gamma,\gamma)$, we prove that the PA property implies MEC, and that the converse holds whenever $\Gamma$ has the PA property. We establish that every left reversible bicancellative monoid and every finitely generated free monoid is MEC, and deduce the PA property for left amenable monoids that are residually a finite group and for finitely generated free monoids. Moreover, for $S=\mathbb F_d^+$, we characterize the free $S$-group as the unique receiving $S$-group for which all fully supported invariant Markov measures on full shifts on finite alphabets admit invariant invertible extensions.

papers.title: Limits of harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
papers.abstract: We give an example of a sequence of positive harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$, that converges pointwise to a non-harmonic function.

papers.title: Automorphism groups of solvable groups of finite abelian ranks
papers.abstract: This paper gives a new explicit construction of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull for virtually solvable groups $\Gamma$ of finite abelian ranks, taking into account the spectrum $S$ of the group $\Gamma$. As an application, we make a detailed study of the structure of $Aut(\Gamma)$ in the finitely generated case and show that a number of natural subgroups are $S$-arithmetic under the condition that $Fitt(\Gamma)$ is $S$-arithmetic. We then proceed by demonstrating that $Out(\Gamma)$ has a $S$-arithmetic image in the group of algebraic outer automorphisms of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull. We finish by discussing further applications of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull towards an open conjecture by Nekrashevych and Pete and topological fixed point theory.

papers.title: Limit groups with respect to Thompson's group $F$ and other hereditarily separating groups
papers.abstract: We prove that a limit group over Thompson's group $F$ cannot be an HNN-extension of $F$ with finitely generated associated subgroup. On the other hand we give an example of an $F$-limit group which is a centralized HNN-extenstions of $F$. We also study relatively limit groups with respect to $F$ and some other known groups of homeomorphisms of topological spaces. This paper revises and extends some results of the second author from arXiv:1308.6330.

papers.title: Bestvina metric and tree reduction for $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture
papers.abstract: We reduce the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture for all Artin groups to properties of Artin groups whose Coxeter diagrams are trees, from which we deduce new classes of Artin groups satisfying the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture. This relies on constructing actions of Artin groups on Bestvina complexes of suitable Garside groupoids.

papers.title: From Trees to Tripods: Proof of $K(\pi,1)$ for Artin groups with $ABI$-type spherical parabolics
papers.abstract: We describe contractibility criteria for typed simplicial complexes modeled on Coxeter diagrams. Such complexes include buildings and also arise as coset complexes of groups with strongly admissible parabolic systems, including Shephard groups, which generalize both Artin and Coxeter groups. Our result applies to a large class of complexes modeled on \emph{tree Coxeter diagrams} and implies deformation retraction onto a nonpositively curved subcomplex. As an application, we reduce the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture for all Artin groups with tree Coxeter diagrams to properties of Artin groups with tripod-shaped Coxeter diagrams. Combining this reduction theorem and properties of braid groups in previous works of Charney, Crisp-McCammond, Haettel and the second named author, we deduce that the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture holds for every Artin group whose spherical parabolic subgroups avoid type $D_n$ ($n \ge 4$) and the exceptional types. We give an analogous tree to tripod reduction for Shephard groups. Our proof relies on two ingredients of independent interest: a notion of combinatorial convexity and a Bestvina-type inequality in certain injective orthoscheme complexes. These ingredients further rely on the use of structural properties of bi-Helly graphs developed in joint work of the first named author with Munro.of bi-Helly graphs (also known as absolute bipartite retracts) developed in joint work of the first named author with Munro.

papers.title: Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $\Gamma$ its long-root geometry, namely $\Gamma$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $\Gamma$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $\Gamma$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $\Gamma$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $\Gamma$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $\Gamma$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $\Gamma$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $\Gamma$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.
